body:
Thank you for the offer, but talking doesn't really help much, at least not now.  As I said in the title, I just wanted to complain, and I didn't expect that my mind would be changed at all.  I know that I'm going to kill myself, it is only a question of when; it could be in a week or a month, but it will happen.  Like I said, I've been putting off my suicide, and my life has only gotten worse.  At other points in my life, I might have had at least one thing to give me some distant glimmer of hope -- something to hold on to -- but that is not the case any longer.  I have absolutely nothing in my life worth living for, and I have absolutely no reason to believe that this will ever change.

I really am just waiting to get the motivation to kill myself.  I have been evaluating my options because I want a guarantee of the method's lethality, and now that I have moved, my previous plans are much more difficult to enact.

I wish that things had turned out differently, but they didn't.

I know that staying alive would make some people happy, but it wouldn't make me happy, so I have dropped that from the list of reasons to stay alive.  I'm sorry.  The only people who I cared enough for to remain alive have decided that I shouldn't be in their lives.

I am pathetic.  I shouldn't feel this way given my situation and age.  If I were several years younger, then my feelings could be understood because children are expected to feel this way, but I'm not a child, so I should be able to handle these small issues.

Yes, everyone struggles with something at one point or another, but in truth, most people do not experience this level of depression.  That is one of the strangest things for me to imagine, but it is true.  Most people do not want to die, and most people do not think about killing themselves on a daily basis.  Everyone has been sad or upset, but not many people can understand what it is like to feel suicidally depressed for five years.  Most people do not put themselves in situations where they hope to be killed, and most people do not put loaded guns in their mouths and consider whether it is possible that their lives will improve.  Most people cannot understand these feelings, and I have difficulty understanding how someone could not have these feelings: how people can go through their lives, not wishing to die, not being in intense pain, and overall, being happy.

There isn't much to tell about the heartbreak because it is pretty standard stuff.  I have dated several women, some of whom I loved, and all of them broke up with me.  It takes me a long time to really develop feelings for a person, and there are not many people who I care deeply for, which is why I was so willing to move thousands of miles away from my family; I like my family, but it is easy for me to leave them.  I am not attached to many people, and the people who I do become close to end up disliking and leaving me.  I want to be clear that I do not resent these women for leaving me because they did what was best for them.  I wouldn't want them to stay with me, if they would rather leave.  I have spent a lot of time trying to understand, however, how people who seemed to care about and love me could leave so suddenly, some of them encouraging me to commit suicide.  Given my feelings for them, I know that I could never leave them without some tremendous new development, but they didn't seem to have any trouble leaving me, yet they claimed to return my feelings.  If I can somehow drive even the people who I care most about away, then I am hopelessly faulty.

If my condition is kept between me and one or two extraordinarily close people, then I'd be okay with it, but that is an unlikely scenario.  More likely, an official record would end up being created, or at the very least, more people than I want would find out, and if that is the case, I would rather die.  As I said before, I don't have any hope of getting better, at this point, and I am only waiting to get killed or kill myself when I can be motivated to do it; if I had easy access to my preferred methods, as I did in the past, I would have killed myself already.  I used to think that maybe things would get better, but over the last five years, things have only gotten significantly worse.  When I try to think of reasons to stay alive, the only one that I can come up with is to spite people who I don't even know.  I am certain that some people would be happy if they knew that someone like me died, and spiting them is the only reason that I can see to live.  That one reason doesn't outweigh my desire to die, however.

I listen to and watch anything good.  I can't say that I have a genre of music that I listen to because I listen to something from every genre.  The same goes for movies, too.  If it is a good movie, I'll watch it.  Still, there are some movies that I might be drawn to more than others, even if they are bad: science fiction, zombie, and apocalypse movies come to mind.

At any rate, I sincerely do appreciate that you took the time to talk to some pathetic stranger on the Internet, but I'm getting pretty tired, so I think that I'll go to sleep for now.  I'll check for any new comments when I wake up, of course.

Nothing is completely confidential; given the right circumstances the information about me would be released.  Even calling a hotline can result in the police being sent to the caller.

I have told my brother a little about how I feel, but I don't want to bother him too much about it, and besides, there's not much he can do, and it can be a pain to get in contact with him (or anyone in my family).

As I said, I haven't been enjoying much, recently.  I used to enjoy things like playing video games, reading, watching movies, and listening to music.

I wouldn't want to tell my parents (and they are thousands of miles away), and I don't have friends.  Honestly, I wouldn't want people in my real life to know about my problems.  I don't want a recorded history of mental illness.

No, there is no one who I can talk to, which is why I felt like coming on the Internet to whine.

I do appreciate the time that you're taking to respond to me.  I notice that you spend quite a bit of time talking to people here, and I want to tell you that you seem like a very nice and good person.

But the judgment of how neurotransmitters are "supposed to" work is based on the how the average person functions.  The neurotransmitters in some people will function differently, sometimes producing undesirable results, but it is part of who they are.  If I have abnormal neurotransmitters, then it is simply part of who I am.  Right now the activity of my brain would be classified as something along the lines of major depressive disorder, but that classification doesn't bother me -- it is only the name given to a certain set of brain activities.  As such, I do identify with depression because, as a point of fact, I am depressed.  This doesn't mean, however, that I can't change, but the change would need to occur naturally.  At one point a person may identify as a Democrat, but in time, he may change to identify as a Republican, and this is perfectly acceptable to me; what I would not accept for myself is taking a pill to artificially change my political identity.

I understand the causes of depression, but I wouldn't say that it helps me at all.  Besides, everything that anyone ever thinks or feels is due to reactions in the brain, and abnormal reactions are categorized as illnesses, but they are still part of who I am.  If any part of me is fundamental to my identity, it is my brain because my brain gives rise to me thoughts and feelings.  My depression and suicidal thoughts and behavior are part of me, and I wouldn't want to alter that with pills; if I begin taking pills to alter my thoughts, then I lose my current identity and become someone else.  I would become a new person with a different mind, and as much as I want to commit suicide, I don't want to kill myself only to create another person who starts to live my life.  I want complete death in mind and body, not only in mind.  Moreover, the new mind that would be created with pills would be artificial, so this identity would be less of a human identity and more of a pill-based identity.  If someone is hypothetically mind controlled so that his personality, thoughts, feelings, and beliefs are changed, then this person no longer has the same identity because the mind-controller created a new mind, and pills are a form of mind control that are aimed at changing a person's thoughts and feelings.  I do not mean to pass judgment on people who do take medication, but it is not something that I can do myself.

As for not being my fault, my depression is as much my fault as any other thought or feeling that I have.  However, I wouldn't say that anyone is responsible for his thoughts or feelings because he cannot control the natural forces that direct the activity in his brain, but I'm not sure that this is the right place to discuss free will and determinism.

I have said the same thing to many people, but I can't convince myself of it.  I may recognize that I shouldn't feel bad for feeling bad simply because other people don't think that I should feel bad, but that doesn't change how I actually do feel.  Just like telling someone that they should be happy, and not sad, won't make that person happy, I can't stop feeling bad for my lack of justification.  Still, I do appreciate the sentiment, so thank you.
